lines.text: Friday evening. You hand three AI agents your backlog and head to dinner. Then one gets stuck. Which one?
Agent R Q puts them all on one task board, each with an owner and a status.
Codex wants to push, so its card jumps to Blocked, with Allow and Deny right on it. One tap, and it carries on.
At dinner, your phone buzzes. Claude Code wants to run a command. Allow Once, and it's back to work.
Monday, nine a.m. The dependency audit already ran, because you scheduled it. Every run is a task you can review.
Best part: over the weekend, Claude learned how to deploy to staging and saved it as a skill. Codex and Antigravity already know it, even that staging needs the VPN.
Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Hermes, and over fifty others. Use whichever agent you like.
Check in from the web, the desktop app, your phone, or the terminal.
Your agents report in, learn from each other, and ask when they need you. It's open source. Try it at Agent R Q dot com.
